And they can't, you know, so we have to go through the laws, and the film of the coast, and I might have to fly up there with, you know... They didn't hear about it. I don't think they did. segments.title: Show opening and Super Bowl visitors in town
segments.summary: Ramsey opens the WDSU Close-Up show with Pete Fountain and Eddie Miller; talk turns to Super Bowl crowds.

segments.title: Celebrity guests at the club and Las Vegas contract
segments.summary: Pete lists visitors at his club (Lombardi, Severinsen, McMahon), then talks about six weeks a year in Vegas and a contract negotiation.

segments.title: Eddie Miller on California versus New Orleans
segments.summary: Eddie says he prefers New Orleans and is happy playing with Pete's band; mentions his kids.

segments.title: New band lineup and labels like Dixieland
segments.summary: Pete describes the added brass and new players, and how critics label his music whatever format he uses.

segments.title: Rock, young musicians and Charlie Brent
segments.summary: Eddie praises the musicianship of young rock groups; Pete praises student arranger Charlie Brent and mentions TV work from Nashville.

segments.title: Godfrey Hirsch's semi-retirement
segments.summary: Godfrey, who left the band, keeps working and even filled in for Lionel Hampton.

segments.title: Listening to the new album and Eddie's own records
segments.summary: They play Spinning Wheel, discuss Eddie and Pete's duet lines, Glenn Campbell's record with Eddie, and a possible Eddie album.

segments.title: Stanley Dance on Eddie as first cool tenor
segments.summary: Ramsey says Stanley Dance called Eddie the first of the cool tenors; Eddie takes it as a compliment.

segments.title: Fishing, the boathouse and a boat accident
segments.summary: Pete talks about fishing and his boathouse; they joke about a boating mishap in which Eddie broke two ribs.

segments.title: Making the album: sweetening and overdubs; break
segments.summary: After playing Traces, Pete explains the first full album with the whole band, with guitar and bass trombone added later; then a station break.

segments.chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
segments.title: Callers about Leon Kelner and Ted Andrews's compliment
segments.summary: A caller asks how long Leon Kelner has played the Roosevelt; Ted Andrews praises Pete's civic cooperation and Jack Sperling's missed visit.

segments.chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
segments.title: An elderly caller invites herself to the club
segments.summary: A 70-year-old woman who has never been in a nightclub chats with Pete, who invites her to hear the music.

segments.chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
segments.title: Walking club costumes and clarinet reeds
segments.summary: Callers ask about the walking club costumes (pilgrims) and Pete's reed strength and brand; Ramsey tells a Paul Desmond joke.

segments.chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
segments.title: Old friend Ellery Mays calls Eddie
segments.summary: Ellery Mays phones Eddie, recalling the 25-cent club, his last New Orleans job; Eddie says he is very happy with Pete's band.

segments.chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
segments.title: Cleaning up Bourbon Street and the Super Bowl
segments.summary: Pete and Ramsey discuss litter cleanup on Bourbon Street and how New Orleans won the Super Bowl effort.

segments.chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
segments.title: WNOE caller on Leon Kelner and hurricane relief
segments.summary: Eddie Deer recalls Leon Kelner's long tenure in the Blue Room and thanks Pete for Hurricane Camille relief.

segments.chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
segments.title: A Closer Walk and Phil Harris at the club
segments.summary: A caller praises Pete's A Closer Walk; Pete says it and The Saints are nightly standards, and mentions Phil Harris.

segments.chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
segments.title: Doc Severinsen expected at the club
segments.summary: Pete and Ramsey talk about Doc Severinsen sitting in, his transformation, and Ed McMahon.

segments.chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
segments.title: Will the big bands come back
segments.summary: Pete says big bands cost too much to keep; Vegas and rock venues are the main outlets; Ellington carries on.

segments.title: Caller praises Pete's tone
segments.summary: An elderly New Orleans trumpeter calls to compliment Pete's tone; Pete says he strives for tone over technique.

segments.title: Pete's clarinet teachers
segments.summary: Pete names teachers including Emmanuel Alexander, Valentino and Johnny Wiggs, his first teacher.

segments.title: Eddie and Pete on tone and Rappolo
segments.summary: Eddie idolized Leon Rappolo's big clarinet tone; Pete says Eddie has the prettiest tenor sound.

segments.title: Requests for Eddie's solo and the network show
segments.summary: A caller asks for an Eddie solo; Pete explains he missed the New Year's network show; they choose to replay Traces.

segments.title: Plans for a nightclub in Jefferson Parish
segments.summary: Pete says he considered new locations after a lease fight on Bourbon Street and might build a bigger place.

segments.title: Traces replayed
segments.summary: Traces is played again with Pete and Eddie.

segments.title: New Orleans jazz festival plans
segments.summary: A caller asks about the summer jazz festival; Pete and Ramsey know little of its status.

segments.title: Lawrence Welk days and red beans and rice
segments.summary: A caller recalls Pete with Lawrence Welk; Pete says he returned for red beans and rice, and callers compare beans.

segments.title: Caller on Hoyt and Dixieland
segments.summary: A short exchange about whether someone was against Dixieland.

segments.title: Old New Orleans sheet music and record company control
segments.summary: A caller suggests reviving old New Orleans jazz publications; Pete says record executives want current hits.

segments.title: New album, Timber Ridge and hurricane damage to family
segments.summary: Pete discusses the new album, a land investment, and his parents riding out the hurricane in Biloxi, causing a cancelled concert and lawsuit.

segments.title: Doc Severinsen broadcast and local TV
segments.summary: A caller asks whether Doc's visit would be broadcast; Pete cites union and record contracts and says local TV is too costly.

segments.title: Eddie on the Crosby alumni band
segments.summary: Eddie says Haggart and Lawson lead a World's Greatest Jazz Band with a Crosby-like sound.

segments.title: Pete's clarinet influences
segments.summary: Pete cites Benny Goodman, Irving Fazola and George Lewis as influences.

segments.title: Sitting in with George Lewis and Tony Almerico; black and white musicians
segments.summary: Pete sat in as a teen with George Lewis and at Tony Almerico's room, and says musicians were first to integrate.

segments.title: Playing what customers want
segments.summary: Pete says club and record pressures force familiar tunes like Up a Lazy River.

segments.title: Tony Almerico and the Junior Dixieland Band
segments.summary: A caller and Pete recall the Parisian Room and Pete's teenage Junior Dixieland Band.

segments.title: Goodbyes and station sign-off
segments.summary: Ramsey thanks the guests, wishes Pete luck with the new club; the announcer closes.
